clue.text: It makes for a bad atmosphere when tart has fall

definitions.text: It makes for a bad atmosphere

parts.note: tart means sour or acid in taste
rain is a fall of water from the sky

explanation.surface: A sour-tempered woman taking a tumble spoils the mood at a gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Polluted precipitation is a symptom and cause of a damaged, unhealthy atmosphere, so it makes the air bad.

clue.text: Even city on the Rhine expels society parasite

parts.note: even means level or flat

indicators.note: expels means the following letter is thrown out of the city's name

parts.note: Worms is a German city on the Rhine

explanation.surface: A level-headed Rhineland town drives out a society sponger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expels' takes S out of WORMS, leaving WORM.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm or fluke is a parasitic flatworm living inside a host animal.

clue.text: See 1
Railway squire disposing of one ill-gotten hoard

indicators.note: ill-gotten suggests something got badly, so the remaining letters are rearranged
disposing of means one letter is thrown out of the fodder

parts.note: taken as written as the anagram fodder
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A country landowner with a railway ditches some ill-gotten gains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' removes one I from RAILWAYSQUIRE, and 'ill-gotten' rearranges the twelve letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel away is to store up secretly, which is what hoarding means as a verb.

clue.text: Prison soldiers set up dotty artist

indicators.note: set up in a down clue means the pieces are read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: can is slang for prison
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are locked up in jail while an eccentric painter stands by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns CAN + GIS into SIGNAC. Paul Signac was a pointillist, painting in dots, hence 'dotty'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Signac was a French pointillist painter whose pictures are built from dots of colour.

clue.text: Like a transgressing Bunter brought before the head (one relishing the unpleasant task)

definitions.text: Like a transgressing Bunter brought before the head
definitions.meaning: Billy Bunter, the greedy schoolboy of British comic stories, is a guzzler, and a pupil sent to the headmaster awaits a caning
someone who seems to enjoy taking on hard or thankless jobs

explanation.surface: A gluttonous schoolboy in trouble is hauled before the headmaster, aside about someone who enjoys drudgery.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the fat, greedy pupil of Greyfriars school in old British comics; a glutton facing a caning gives the literal first reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who keeps taking on hardship or tough work as though enjoying it.

clue.text: Streep needs year off to overcome drink

indicators.note: off means the letter for year comes away from the actress's first name

parts.note: Meryl Streep is the American actress

indicators.note: overcome in a down clue reads as come over, so the word to is turned upside down

explanation.surface: The actress Meryl Streep must take a year away to conquer her drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes Y from MERYL, leaving MERL; 'overcome' turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Merlot is a red wine grape and the wine made from it, a common drink.

clue.text: A solemn, if moving, setting of Douglas

indicators.note: moving means the letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A grave, emotional musical arrangement of a piece by someone called Douglas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges ASOLEMNIF. Douglas is the capital of the island, not a composer whose work is being set.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas is the capital town of the island in the Irish Sea, so the island is its setting.

clue.text: She knocks back Guinness and gets one in

indicators.note: gets one in means the numeral is put inside
knocks back means the actor's first name is turned backwards

parts.note: Alec Guinness was the British actor
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A woman downs a pint of Guinness and buys a round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocks back' turns ALEC into CELA, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Celia is a woman's name, so it can stand for any she in a clue.

clue.text: Liberal line in jokes — accommodating measure once used by writers

indicators.note: accommodating means the word for jokes takes in a further piece
in means the two letters are put inside the word for jokes

parts.note: quips are witty jokes
an en is a printer's measure of width

explanation.surface: A liberal sprinkling of gags suits a style of writing from the past.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers in one clue: the jokes take the Liberal line in first, then make room for the printer's measure further along.
explanation.definitionFit: Feather pens cut from quills were the writing tools of earlier centuries before steel nibs.

clue.text: Imprisonment causes, it's said, Jack strain

indicators.note: it's said means the words are heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: jack is slang for a detective, shortened DET, and strain is tension

explanation.surface: Being locked up, people say, puts a great strain on a man called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is old slang for a detective, written DET; DET TENSION said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Detention is the state of being held in custody, a form of confinement.

clue.text: Spanish men's accent

parts.note: the Spanish word for gentlemen, senores, carries a wavy mark over its n

explanation.surface: The way Spanish men pronounce their words.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a manner of speaking; the accent meant is the written mark above the n in the Spanish words for men.
explanation.definitionFit: The wavy mark over the Spanish letter n is called a tilde, a written diacritic.

clue.text: One who feels way outside United Fish

indicators.note: outside means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: one who gropes is feeling his way blind

explanation.surface: A blind man fumbling around a football team member, with fish involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts GROPER round U.
explanation.definitionFit: A grouper is a large sea fish of the sea bass family.

clue.text: No longer tender, tip of finger when dipped in butter

indicators.note: dipped in means the letter is put inside the animal

parts.note: a goat butts, so it is a butter

indicators.note: tip of here means the end letter of the word finger

explanation.surface: A fingertip dunked into a pat of butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one who butts, a GOAT, not the dairy spread; 'dipped in' puts R, the last letter of 'finger', inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The groat was an old English fourpenny coin, long since withdrawn as legal tender.

clue.text: See 6
Native American confectionery piece Tyler brought back

parts.note: a choc is a piece of chocolate confectionery

indicators.note: brought back means the rebel's first name is turned backwards

parts.note: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381

explanation.surface: A Native American is handed a sweet that someone called Tyler brought home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns WAT into TAW. Wat Tyler led the 1381 Peasants' Revolt in England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Choctaw are an Indigenous people of the south-eastern United States.

clue.text: Prone to cry "Insignificant party's artless!"

parts.note: wee means tiny or insignificant

indicators.note: artless means the word art is taken out of the word for party

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter, so this is party

explanation.surface: A tearful person dismisses a small, unsophisticated gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artless' removes ART from PARTY, leaving PY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone weepy is tearful, inclined to shed tears easily.

clue.text: See 8
Multiple occupancy housing starry group

indicators.note: housing means the answer sits inside these words

explanation.surface: Shared accommodation for a crowd of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' signals the answer inside multipLE Occupancy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Be more canny than to publicly expose pain

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them publicly
smart means a stinging pain

explanation.surface: Exposing someone's hurt in public is a way to get one over on them.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsmart someone is to outwit them, being cleverer than they are.

clue.text: Lie with non-anglicised Ray Cotton?

parts.note: a fib is a small lie
ray is the English spelling of the sol-fa note re

explanation.surface: Telling a lie about a man named Ray Cotton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ray' looks like a first name before 'Cotton', but it is the sol-fa note, spelt RE in its original form.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is an example of a textile fibre, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Like porno films? Then ring producer, flower!

parts.note: blue films are pornographic ones
a bell is what makes a ringing sound

explanation.surface: An outraged viewer calls the maker of dirty films.
explanation.definitionFit: The bluebell is a woodland spring flower with blue bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: "Nature Determined" prepared for publication

parts.note: type means nature or kind
set means determined or resolved

explanation.surface: A headline from a science magazine named Nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Typesetting arranges text into type ready for printing.

clue.text: Place like Outer Mongolia, it's in the blood

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: Outer means the first and last letters of Mongolia

explanation.surface: A remote spot such as Outer Mongolia is in someone's ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale fluid part of blood that carries the cells.

clue.text: Cover for members getting drunk on Sunday

parts.note: tight is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A club's insurance for its members is spent on a Sunday drinking session.
explanation.definitionFit: Tights are a garment covering the legs, here called members, or limbs.

clue.text: A resort of sound film, audio-wise

indicators.note: audio-wise means the word is heard spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a talkie is an early film with sound

explanation.surface: A seaside town known for its film soundtracks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TALKIE and the answer sound alike. TORQUAY is an English seaside resort in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquay is a seaside resort town on the Devon coast in England.

clue.text: Warning: branch lies outside city

indicators.note: lies outside means the first piece is placed around the second

parts.note: an arm is a branch, as of a river or organisation
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A notice says a local office is just beyond the city limits.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal that warns of danger.

clue.text: See 4
Cooks rub a magic food thickening ingredient

indicators.note: cooks means the letters are worked over into a new form, as with cooking the books

explanation.surface: A chef massages a magic ingredient into the dish to thicken it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooks' rearranges RUBAMAGIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum arabic is acacia sap used as a stabiliser and thickener in food.

clue.text: "Convalescence is something useful to snooker players", snooker player said

parts.note: a rest is the cue support used in snooker for long shots

indicators.note: said means the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a cuer is someone wielding a cue, a snooker player

explanation.surface: A snooker player claims that recovery is a handy tool for the game.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker is a British table game played with cues; the rest supports the cue, and CUER said aloud gives CURE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest cure is a period of complete rest prescribed for recovery from illness.

clue.text: See 28
Dispense with pointless church building, making a pile

indicators.note: pointless means the compass point E is removed

parts.note: to axe something is to dispense with it
a minster is a large church building

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a useless church building creates a heap of rubble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pointless' removes E, a compass point, from AXE, leaving AX.
explanation.definitionFit: Axminster is a type of woven carpet, which has a pile, so the answer is named by its feature.

clue.text: From our star turn, Los Amigos: "Roof Tops"

indicators.note: turn means the word Los is read backwards
Tops means the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A band called Los Amigos plays a song called Roof Tops at a sunny festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses LOS to SOL; 'Tops' takes A and R from Amigos and Roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means relating to the sun, which is our nearest star.
